heading: ஆங்கில மொழிபெயர்ப்பு
lines: Like a fine-tusked elephant in rut
Rearing its trunk aloft in the manner
Of the goad it would no longer heed,
My wisdom and composed manner
And self-restraint and sense of shame
Becoming worthless;
And others laughing at my weakness,
Appearing before me
Like lightning flash or like a dream,
Showing itself yet hiding,
Throwing my heart out of me,
That woman who has kept her own beauty from me,
How am I to reach her?
With strings of peacock feather jewels
And lovely flowers of pūḷai, āvirai and erukkam
Binding and twisting the garland
And singing before all in the town square:
'Listen to me all of you:
This affliction I am in,
And this horse of palmyra stems
Are the ones
That woman with glittering ornaments has given me
Whom I've lost my heart to.
My forbearance breaching the bounds,
My life goes wasting away,
Swimming on the undoing waters of passion
This damsel of comely forehead afflicted me with,
Like the doll made of salt
Into a salt-pan flung,
Dissolving in.
Pūḷai and the golden āvirai are the flowers
That damsel of shoulders bamboo's grace excelling
Has gifted me with.
I've been drowned
In the burning ailment of passion
That goes beyond the bounds of my bearing,
That brings my native features to nought,
Which that damsel with radiant jewels handed me
And my life goes wearing away in paces
Like the wax flung into the boiling ghee.
Concern for this affliction of mine
Did come from the strangers and the little ones.
My song reaching out to her,
That woman of kindly tongue there came
And the bliss of her love extended;
'This palmyra horse, a companion in distress,
Shall hold no bearing with me around'
Said she with solicitousness felt.
It all came like
The men of tranquil bearing
Given to arduous austerities
Coming freed of their bodily frame,
And gaining access to the paradisal home.
V. Murugan
